look_here_first: Look into the flower center: A. incanum has a pubescent staminal column and a 5-branched style. The small corolla is often reflexed and yellow or pink with a dark red center; fruit stays compact rather than forming the long-spined velvetleaf crown.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current FNA/POWO range treatment does not support Texas as native for this species. It remains in the learner because it is in the approved source pool and is useful for identifying or correcting a possible local misidentification.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Not confirmed target-zone native. Treat local Hays signals as an ID/re-identification cue, not native-range evidence.

best_field_traits: small yellow or pink flowers often dark-centered
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The expected Texas look-alike A. fruticosum usually has plain yellow flowers and 6–9 style branches.
morphology_keys.flower: Calyx 3–5 mm; corolla reflexed, yellow or pink with dark red center, petals 4–6 mm; staminal column pubescent; style 5-branched.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Schizocarp cask-shaped, not medially constricted, 7–9 × 6 mm; mericarp apex acute/apiculate, tomentulose; 3 seeds per mericarp, seeds ~2 mm.

comparisons.key_distinctions: The expected Texas look-alike A. fruticosum usually has plain yellow flowers and 6–9 style branches.
